## Overview

This vignette demonstrates the end-to-end haploStack workflow starting from
**SelectionTools (ST) numeric genotype files**.  ST genotypes store diploid
calls as marker-coded values (e.g. `1/4`, `4/4`) with markers as rows and
samples as columns.

```
Input files                     Output artefacts
──────────────────────────────  ──────────────────────────────────────────
my_genotype.csv (ST format)     GenoMeta object (in memory)
my_map.txt                      Haplotype profile (.rds)
my_blocks.txt                   Block location table (.csv)
my_effects_yield.GS.Eff         Local-GEBV matrix (.txt per trait)
                                Format-converted genotype files (.ped / .csv)
                                Plots (Manhattan, block-counts, alignment)
```

---

## 1  Input file formats

### 1.1  Genotype file (SelectionTools CSV)

Markers as rows, samples as columns.  Cell values use the ST numeric encoding
(A→1, G→2, C→3, T→4) as slash-separated haplotypes:

```
Marker   S001   S002   S003   ...
SNP_001  1/4    1/1    4/4    ...
SNP_002  2/2    2/3    3/3    ...
```

The file may be tab or comma delimited.  The first column is treated as marker
names; the remaining columns are samples.

### 1.2  Map file (`.txt`)

Three columns with a header — order: Marker | Chrom | Pos (bp):

```
Marker    Chrom  Pos
SNP_001   1H     12340000
SNP_002   1H     18920000
```

### 1.3  Block file (optional)

Either **coordinate format** (Chrom, Block, Start, End) or
**marker-level format** (Chrom, Marker, Block) — tab-delimited with header.

### 1.4  Effect file (`.GS.Eff` or plain `.txt`)

Three columns, no header — Marker | Allele | Effect:

```
SNP_001  1   0.0412
SNP_002  2  -0.0187
```

Allele codes must match the ST encoding (`"1"` = A, `"2"` = G, etc.).

---

## 2  Read genotype data

```{r read-st}
library(haploStack)
library(data.table)

# ── Read ST genotype + map (and optionally a block file) ──────────────────────
meta <- read_st_genotype(
  file       = "data/my_genotype.csv",
  map_file   = "data/my_map.txt",
  block_file = "data/my_blocks.txt",   # omit if attaching blocks separately
  pos_unit   = "bp"
)

is_geno_meta(meta)   # TRUE

cat("Samples :", meta$metadata$n_samples,  "\n")
cat("Markers :", meta$metadata$n_markers,  "\n")
cat("Encoding:", paste(names(meta$metadata$char_dict), collapse = ", "), "\n")

# Array shape: (n_samples, n_markers, ploidy=2)
dim(meta$geno_arrays)
head(meta$map_info)
```

---

## 3  Build GenoMeta from in-memory objects (alternative)

If your genotype data is already loaded as an R matrix — from another tool or
custom preprocessing — use `build_geno_meta()` instead of a file reader.  It
accepts both ST-style slash-separated matrices and wide-allele matrices
(one column per allele, as produced by PLINK allele extraction).

```{r build-from-memory}
# Example: ST-style matrix already in memory
geno_mat <- read.csv("data/my_genotype.csv", row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
map_df   <- read.table("data/my_map.txt",   header = TRUE)

meta_mem <- build_geno_meta(
  geno_2d      = as.matrix(geno_mat),   # markers × samples OR samples × markers
  map          = map_df,
  ploidy       = 2L,
  split_char   = "/",   # "/" for ST slash-separated; "" for two-char concat
  source_format = "selectiontools"
)

is_geno_meta(meta_mem)
dim(meta_mem$geno_arrays)
```

---

## 4  Attach block information (if not loaded with the reader)

Skip this step if you passed `block_file` to `read_st_genotype()` above.

```{r attach-blocks}
block_map <- fread("data/my_blocks.txt")
meta      <- attach_block_info(meta, block_source = block_map)

# Confirm blocks attached
head(meta$block_marker_map_info)
nrow(meta$block_info)
```

---

## 5  Build block location table

```{r block-location}
bloc <- build_block_location_info(
  meta,
  output_dir = "output",
  prefix     = "barley_st"
)

# Chrom, Block, Start, End, Pos (midpoint), Num_SNPs, Block_length
print(bloc$block_info)
```

---

## 6  Derive profile views from the GenoMeta

`meta` is the single central object. Derive the denormalised profile views
(wide allele table, marker/block metadata) on demand with `geno_meta_views()`.

```{r profile}
profile <- geno_meta_views(meta)

cat("Encoding :", profile$encoding,           "\n")
cat("Samples  :", length(profile$samples),    "\n")
cat("Blocks   :", nrow(profile$block_meta),   "\n")
cat("Markers  :", nrow(profile$marker_meta),  "\n")

# Allele table: rows = samples × ploidy, cols = markers
head(profile$alleles[, 1:8, with = FALSE])

# Persist the GenoMeta
save_geno_meta(meta, "output/barley_st_geno_meta.rds")
```

---

## 7  Compute local GEBVs

```{r effects}
# ── Single trait ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
eff_yield <- read_effect_file("data/effects_yield.GS.Eff")

gebv_yield <- compute_profile_localgebv(
  profile        = profile,
  effect_df      = eff_yield,
  level          = "genotype",   # "haplotype" for per-haplotype resolution
  center_by_freq = TRUE
)

cat("GEBV matrix:", dim(gebv_yield), "(blocks × samples + 1)\n")
print(gebv_yield[1:5, 1:6, with = FALSE])

fwrite(gebv_yield, "output/gebv_yield.txt", sep = "\t")
```

---

## 8  Run the full catalogue (multi-trait)

```{r catalogue}
effect_list <- list(
  Yield    = read_effect_file("data/effects_yield.GS.Eff"),
  Protein  = read_effect_file("data/effects_protein.GS.Eff"),
  Maturity = read_effect_file("data/effects_maturity.GS.Eff")
)

results <- run_haplotype_catalogue(
  geno_meta      = meta,
  effect_list    = effect_list,
  output_dir     = "output/catalogue_st",
  ld_threshold   = 0.5,
  save_profile   = TRUE,
  center_by_freq = TRUE,
  n_cores        = 1L
)

names(results)            # one element per trait
names(results$Yield)      # gebv_matrix, gebv_summary, block_counts, profile
```

Files written to `output/catalogue_st/`:

| File | Content |
|------|---------|
| `haplotype_profile_0.5_t0.rds` | Serialised haplotype profile |
| `Haplotype_GA_Matrix_*_Yield.txt` | Block × Sample GEBV matrix |
| `GEBV_*_Yield.txt` | Per-sample total GEBV |
| `Block_Counts_*_Yield.txt` | Positive / zero / negative block counts |
| `Manhattan_Variance_*_Yield.png` | Per-block effect variance |
| `Manhattan_Effect_*_Yield.png` | Per-sample effect distribution |
| `Block_Counts_Yield.png` | Stacked bar chart |

---

## 9  Visualise results

```{r plots, eval=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
library(ggplot2)

# ── Manhattan — effect variance ───────────────────────────────────────────────
block_var <- results$Yield$gebv_matrix |>
  data.table::melt(id.vars = "Block", variable.name = "Sample",
                   value.name = "Effect") |>
  merge(bloc$block_info[, .(Block, Chrom, Pos)], by = "Block") |>
  (\(dt) dt[, .(BlockVariance = var(Effect, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(Block, Chrom, Pos)])()

p_var <- plot_manhattan_variance(block_var, trait_name = "Yield")
print(p_var)
ggsave("output/Manhattan_Variance_Yield.png", p_var, width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 150)

# ── Block counts per sample ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
p_counts <- plot_block_counts(results$Yield$block_counts, trait_name = "Yield")
print(p_counts)
ggsave("output/Block_Counts_Yield.png", p_counts, width = 12, height = 6, dpi = 150)

# ── Haplotype alignment — chromosome 1H ──────────────────────────────────────
meta_1H  <- filter_geno_meta(meta, chromosomes = list(list(chr = "1H")))
p_align  <- plot_haplotype_alignment(meta_1H, show_block_boundaries = TRUE,
                                      show_block_labels = TRUE)
print(p_align)
ggsave("output/Alignment_1H.png", p_align, width = 14, height = 8, dpi = 150)
```

---

## 10  Filter the GenoMeta

```{r filter}
# ── Chromosome region ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
meta_1H <- filter_geno_meta(
  meta,
  chromosomes = list(list(chr = "1H", start = 0, end = 300e6))
)

# ── Specific samples and blocks ───────────────────────────────────────────────
elite    <- c("S001", "S002", "S010", "S020")
top_blks <- profile$block_meta[order(-n_markers)][1:10, block_id]

meta_sub <- filter_geno_meta(meta, keep_samples = elite, blocks = top_blks)
prof_sub <- geno_meta_views(meta_sub)
cat("Subset GenoMeta:", length(prof_sub$samples), "samples,",
    nrow(prof_sub$block_meta), "blocks\n")
```

---

## 11  Export genotypes in other formats

Convert a SelectionTools genotype into PLINK PED or genomicSimulation format.

```{r export}
# ── ST → PLINK PED ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
write_geno_meta(meta, path = "output/genotype_plink", output_format = "plink_ped")
# Writes: output/genotype_plink.ped + output/genotype_plink.map

# ── ST → genomicSimulation CSV ────────────────────────────────────────────────
write_geno_meta(meta, path = "output/genotype_gs.csv", output_format = "gs")

# ── Inspect the ST matrix (markers × samples, "1/4" cells) ───────────────────
converted_st <- geno_meta_to_matrix(meta, output_format = "st")
dim(converted_st$matrix)         # n_markers × n_samples
converted_st$matrix[1:4, 1:5]

# ── Inspect the PLINK matrix (samples × markers, "A T" space-sep cells) ──────
converted_pl <- geno_meta_to_matrix(meta, output_format = "plink_ped")
dim(converted_pl$matrix)         # n_samples × n_markers
converted_pl$matrix[1:3, 1:4]

# ── Re-encode the GenoMeta: ST numeric → nucleotide letters ──────────────────
meta_nuc <- recode_geno_meta(meta, to_type = "nucleotide")
meta_nuc$metadata$encoding     # "nucleotide"
geno_meta_views(meta_nuc)$alleles[1:2, 1:6, with = FALSE]
```

---

## 12  Load a saved GenoMeta in a new session

```{r reload}
meta2 <- load_geno_meta("output/barley_st_geno_meta.rds")
meta2$metadata$encoding
nrow(meta2$sample_info)
```
